summary: Paul Tedesco was a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, Indological, and linguistic studies. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Vienna under Bernhard Geiger, later holding posts at the Institute for Advanced Study, Princeton, and Yale University.

Paul Theodor Hoffmann worked in Indology, philosophy, and other fields. He studied at Munich, Grenoble Alpes, Humboldt Berlin, and Tübingen, earning his Ph.D. under Richard von Garbe, and directed the Theaterwissenschaftliches Institut at the University of Hamburg in 1941.

Paul Thieme worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Emil Sieg, Heinrich Lüders, Wilhelm Schulze, and Kamalakanta Mishra. His academic posts included Allahabad, Breslau, Berlin, Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg, Frankfurt, Yale, and Tübingen.

Paul Tillich was a philosopher and theologian who completed degrees at Halle-Wittenberg and Breslau. He held teaching posts at Berlin, Marburg, TU Dresden, Leipzig, Frankfurt, Union Theological Seminary, Harvard, and the University of Chicago.
Paul W. Kroll is a sinologist who studied at the University of Michigan. Around 1980 to 1988, he served as Associate Professor of Chinese and department chair at the University of Colorado Boulder.

Paul Whalley was an Indologist and historian who earned his B.A. and M.A. at Trinity College, Cambridge. He served in the Bengal Civil Service from 1860 to 1890 and was Secretary to the Ministry of Home Affairs.
Paul Wilfred O'Brien was a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his Ph.D. at the University of California, Berkeley. He later taught at the Pontifical College of St. Pius X from 1958 to 1965.

Paul Williams specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. After earning degrees from Sussex and Oxford, he was a Bowra Research Fellow at Wadham College, held a visiting chair at Calgary, and became Emeritus Professor at the University of Bristol.
Paul Wodilla was an Indologist who studied at Comenius University and completed his Ph.D. at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg between approximately 1925 and 1928.

Paul de Lagarde worked in religious studies, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Berlin and Halle under Friedrich Rückert and August Tholuck, later holding posts at Halle and the University of Göttingen.

Paul-Émile Dumont was an Indologist who studied at Brussels and Bologna, also training under Francesco Lorenzo Pullè, Willem Caland, Hermann Oldenberg, and Paul Deussen. He held posts at Brussels, Kiel, and Johns Hopkins University.

Paula Arai is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who earned degrees from Kalamazoo College and Harvard. She held faculty appointments at Vanderbilt, Carleton College, and Louisiana State University, and became professor at the Institute of Buddhist Studies.

Paulina Kolata works in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies, earning her PhD from the University of Manchester. She held posts at Chester, Manchester, Manchester Metropolitan, Copenhagen, and Lund, before becoming Assistant Professor at Harvard in 2025.
Paulina Koniuch is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. She completed her bachelor's degree at the University of Warsaw from 2017 to 2020 and joined its faculty in 2023.

Paulinus of St. Bartholomew was an Indologist and linguist who studied in Prague and Rome. He served at the Malabar Mission, became Rector at Saint Joseph's Pontifical Seminary, and held posts at Collegio San Pancrazio and the Pontifical Urban University.
Pavankumar Satuluri specializes in computational linguistics and Indology. He has held academic posts at Chinmaya Vishwavidyapeeth and the Indian Institute of Technology Roorkee.

Pavel Grintser was an Indologist who studied at Moscow State University under Mikhail Nikolayevich Peterson. He held long-term posts at the Gorky Institute of World Literature and the Russian State University for the Humanities.

Pavel Jakovlevič Petrov was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Moscow, St. Petersburg, and under Robert Lenz and Franz Bopp. He served as professor of Sanskrit at Kazan University and professor of Oriental languages at Moscow State University.

Pavel Konstantinovich Portnyagin worked in Iranian, Central Asian, and Tibetan studies. He studied at the Pontifical Gregorian University in 1932 and was employed as a translator at the Uzbek Karakul Sheep Breeding Research Institute.

Pavel Poucha was an Indologist, linguist, and Central Asian studies scholar. He earned his PhD at Charles University under Vincenc Lesný and Oldřich Hujer, and later served as a Docent at the Oriental Institute of the Czech Academy of Sciences.
